submission.natural_language_explanation: Previous-token head that crosses 0.25 x max only when it attends almost entirely to the token just before, which happens when the current token is a tightly bound continuation of that token. It is strongest (0.5-1.0 x max) on the second and later pieces of a word or name split into subwords (Mac|mill|an, Mc|Av|oy, App|les, Sch|i|weck), the second of two newline or whitespace-run tokens (blank lines, deep indentation), an abbreviation's period (U|.|S|., p|.), and the word after ' there' (there is/are/'s/will be). It is weaker (0.25-0.5 x max) on stock collocations such as do not, can be, have/need/try to, part of, such as, more than, Thank you and ', which', and on verbs and nouns in the first three or four tokens of a short text. Every other token stays under the line: any token right after ' the', ' a', ' in', ' for', ' with', ' this', ',', '.' or a sentence-opening 'The', every sentence-final '.', and free adjective+noun or noun+verb combinations in prose and code. So a sentence built only from common one-token words in determiner+noun and preposition+noun phrases (e.g. 'The house is near the park.') is predicted inactive.
